{"id": "2:30/q03", "question": "What governs إذ and how does it function grammatically?", "turns_on": "Whether idh contributes temporal meaning and which stated or implied clause governs it.", "positions": [{"id": "2:30/q03/p1", "position": "Idh is redundant", "reasons": "IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB (author): Introductory idh is extra, so the Lord said. IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL (author): Idh may be extra in 2:30 and 31:13. IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL (author): Ibn Mayyada's line is poetry evidence for extra idh. NAHHAS (أبو عبيدة): Abū ʿUbayda says «إذ» is a temporal adverb and is not an extra word. MAWARDI-FULL (author): Alternatively, إذ is not extra: the omitted sense is “He began your creation when,” with ذهب understood after the poet’s أينما. BAGHAWI-FULL (author): The phrase may mean And your Lord said, with idh redundant, or may mean Remember when your Lord said; this explains similar Quranic constructions. IBNATIYYA-FULL (معمر بن المثنى): Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā says the particle idh is redundant, yielding the sense “and your Lord said.” IBNATIYYA-FULL (أبو إسحاق الزجاج): Al-Zajjāj calls Abū ʿUbayda’s claim that idh is redundant an audacious interpretation; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says all exegetes rejected it. TABRISI (أبو عبيدة): Abu Ubayda calls إذ extra; al-Zajjaj and others reject this because a particle that adds sound meaning cannot be discarded. IBNJAWZI-ZAD (أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة): Abū ʿUbayda, followed by Ibn Qutayba, treats idh as redundant, yielding ‘and your Lord said.’ RAZI-FULL (بعض الناس): One view treats إذ as an extra particle customary in Arabic; Razi rejects it because the Qur'an contains nothing without meaning. QURTUBI-FULL (أبو عبيدة): Abu ʿUbayda (Maʿmar ibn al-Muthanna) takes idh as redundant; al-Qurtubi rejects this, following the grammarians and exegetes. BAYDAWI-FULL (معمر): Maʿmar regards إذ as extra. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (أبو عبيدة): Abū ʿUbayda and Ibn Qutayba take idh as redundant; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this and criticizes their grammatical competence. SAMIN-DURR (أبو عبيد): A fifth analysis treats إذ as redundant, attributed to Abu Ubayd. SAMIN-DURR (author): إذ is not declinable except when attached to a time noun, is not a direct object despite many grammarians' analysis, and is not a place adverb, redundant, causal particle or suddenness particle. IBNKATHIR-FULL (أبو عبيدة): Abu ʿUbayda claimed idh is extra, making the sense simply “And your Lord said”; Ibn Jarir rejects this, as do all exegetes, and al-Zajjaj calls it rash. BURHAN (قيل): Some treat إذ in the creation account as extra; another analysis takes it to mean قد. ALUSI-FULL (author): Idh generally remains adverbial, though grammarians dispute whether it can be an object, causal particle, suddenness marker, place adverb, or redundant; al-Baḥr denies those uses outside contextual implication. ALUSI-FULL (المعربون): Grammarians variously call idh redundant or equivalent to qad, place it as a subject or an object of an omitted verb, attach it to earlier wording, or connect it to dhikr. ZAJJAJ (أبو عبيدة): Abū ʿUbayda calls idh redundant; al-Zajjāj rejects this as reckless because idh is a noun meaning ‘time.’ IBNJAWZI-ZAD (الزجاج وابن القاسم): Al-Zajjāj and Ibn al-Qāsim reject the claim that idh is redundant; al-Zajjāj takes it to mean ‘at the time’ of the beginning of creation. QURTUBI-FULL (الزجاج والنحاس): Al-Zajjaj, al-Nahhas, and the exegetes reject Abu ʿUbayda: idh is a temporal noun, not an extra particle. ABUHAYYAN-FULL (author): Idh cannot be an object, causal or sudden particle, loca
